text:
CHI comes to Boston having lost four of five, outscored 16-6, and 2 days ago fell 4-1 at DET even though Viktor Arvidsson scored three goals. BOS lost 4-1 at STL in its last game and is 2-2-1 over its last five. The Bruins' results are ahead of their chances (a +18 goal difference on +0.6 expected), with finishing and goaltending doing the lifting. CHI is the opposite: a -21 goal difference on -11.8 expected, so it has been better than its record.

Still, BOS has controlled more of the play. At five on five it has taken 53% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), against 40% for CHI. Our model has BOS at 3.35 expected goals tonight and CHI at 2.77. The Bruins take 4.6 penalties a game, which keeps handing out power plays. In net, Jeremy Swayman (projected) is +6.6 in goals saved above expected this season and +26.5 last year. Arvid Soderblom (projected, in for Spencer Knight) is at -2.8 this season and -4.7 last.

For CHI, Connor Bedard is 70% for a point with a 4-game point streak, and Patrick Kane is one assist from 900. For BOS, David Pastrnak is 80% for a point. Our under-the-radar picks, as players to watch: Casey Mittelstadt, whose shots have been dangerous (2.5 expected goals in his last 10 games), and Roman Kantserov, who is 52% for a point as his line creates chances.
